item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00505","case1_error":"Evaluates 48 − 17 − 10 as 11 instead of 21, understating remaining inventory and profit.","case2_error":"Omits the third supplier’s 2,500,000 cars when totaling allocations to the first three suppliers.","reason":"Case 1 miscalculates a correctly written subtraction; case 2 leaves a required allocation out of the total.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00506","case1_error":"Divides among four siblings instead of five people including Jose.","case2_error":"Treats all three initial packs as packs given away, despite the question specifying one pack.","reason":"Case 1 excludes a participant from the divisor; case 2 confuses initial inventory with the amount transferred.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00507","case1_error":"Applies only two halvings over 30 years, incorrectly assigning the first halving to age 20.","case2_error":"Leading answer marker says 14, but the derivation correctly calculates the requested combined size as 21.","reason":"Case 2 has only an answer-marker conflict, so a shared mathematical error cannot be established.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J00508","case1_error":"Subtracts six inches from rim height instead of adding them to determine the required reach.","case2_error":"Uses the $11 discount amount as the boots’ purchase price instead of subtracting it from $110.","reason":"Case 1 reverses the direction of a height offset; case 2 substitutes a discount amount for the remaining price.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00509","case1_error":"Counts only one climb of Reece’s ladder, omitting the multiplier for his 15 climbs.","case2_error":"Calculates grooming time for one dog, omitting the multiplier for two dogs.","reason":"Both omit a required multiplicity factor, counting one instance where the question specifies several.","judgment":"same"}]}
